headline: Deadlocked reaches 4.13% after PAL batches are corrected for NTSC-U
summary: Deadlocked's NTSC-U v1.00 matched code rose from 2.42% to 4.13%, with 2,019 of 15,056 functions reported finished. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. Shared object and multiplayer-menu batches initially checked only on PAL receive a follow-up audit against NTSC-U.
highlights: #7 through #16 bring shared helpers, menu handlers, serializers and option routines.
The NTSC-U follow-up corrects region-specific thresholds and call targets, renames one misplaced routine and moves two unsupported functions to near misses.
#6 adds another broad batch of game and shared-level implementations.
#5 makes build and candidate-checking tools run natively on Windows.
